entry.dc:title: KRUPP TRANSPORT CRAWLERS - A NEW AID IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Krumrey A.
entry.dc:description: A heavy-load crawler for transporting loads of up to 1,000 tons has been designed and built. The principal technical data of four designs are shown.

entry.dc:title: Creation of Safe and Healthy Condition of Labor for Soviet Coal Miners - A Most Important Social Task.
entry.dc:creator: Nikitin V.
entry.dc:description: The measures taken in the USSR to improve the state of safety engineering and to make the conditions of work at the coal industry undertakings safer are described. Mechanization of mining work and conveyor transport reduce the number of injuries. So does open-pit mining which will constitute 36% of total output in 1980. Underground mining encounters increasing difficulties owing to greater depths and more complicated geological conditions. Degassing is carried out at 196 mines, with extraction of 1. 3 billion m**3 of methane per annum. Measures to prevent and control coal, rock, and gas bursts are described.

entry.dc:title: INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES EMPLOYED TO CONSTRUCT SLURRY CUTOFF TRENCH FOR SYNCRUDE'S BEAVER CREEK DAM.
entry.dc:creator: Brown M.
entry.dc:description: Syncrude Canada Ltd. recently completed construction of its ambitious tar-sand mining and processing facilities at Mildred Lake, Alberta. The Syncrude operation involves the open-pit mining of approximately 270,000 tonnes (300,000 tons) of tar sand daily using draglines and a conveyor system. The peat deposits and high groundwater levels at the site combine to make the excavation and construction of a conventional rolled clay cutoff impractical. For these reasons, the slurry cutoff trench technique described here was utilized to produce an efficient and effective seepage cutoff under various sections of the Beaver Creek Dam.

entry.dc:title: The Bingham copper deposits, Utah, as an exploration target: History and pre-excavation geology
entry.dc:creator: James L.P.
entry.dc:description: The Bingham mining district was discovered in 1863, shortly after Caucasian civilization reached the Great Basin. For many decades argentiferous galena-sphalerite ores were produced from steeply dipping veins and bedded replacement deposits. Copper occurrences were known, but largely uneconomic. Recognition of the copper- rich mineralized porphyry body at the center of the district had occurred by the end of the 19th century. Breakthroughs in mining technology were required to make the deposit minable, but once begun the mine rapidly became the largest in the northern hemisphere. Large contact metasomatic copper deposits also were developed in limestone units adjacent to the Bingham stock. A number of careful workers, both famous and forgotten, contributed to the general knowledge of base metal deposits at Bingham. A major lawsuit led to careful studies of the replacement deposits by noted experts. Prior to mining, the Bingham porphyry copper deposit was characterized by a leached, iron oxide-rich capping, typically containing several tenths of one percent copper and also traces of gold. Telluride minerals were present locally. Coarse placer gold and boulders of ferruginous conglomerate occurred in adjacent drainages. The larger high-grade veins of the district radiated from or occurred near the boundaries of the mineralized portion of the stock. Deep underground workings followed lead-zinc ores to 5,000 feet vertically beneath the surface and work is now in progress to mine copper ores below the 3,300-foot level of the old underground mines. Open-pit mining has reached depths of 2,500 feet below the original outcrops. The district contains a very barren pluton (Last Chance stock) and a metal zoning pattern that extends only relatively short distances outward into country rock. A few square miles of gravel cover could have effectively concealed the highly economic copper-rich center of the district.

entry.dc:title: Athabasca tar sands: Occurrence and commercial projects
entry.dc:creator: Spragins F.
entry.dc:description: This chapter focuses on the Athabasca tar-sand deposit of northeastern Alberta, Canada, and the commercial developments going on there. The Athabasca tar sands are the major deposit of oil in a viscous-oil trend, stretching across Alberta, from the Alberta-Saskatchewan border near Cold Lake to a point near the town of Peace River. The Athabasca tar sands are divided into two zones: one where oil deposits are covered by oil-barren surface deposits of from 0 to 150 ft and one where these overburden deposits range from 150 ft to more than 2000 ft in thickness. A number of oil companies have undertaken several commercial projects in the area. The Syncrude project has been designed to produce 125,000 bbl/day of synthetic crude oil. In the Syncrude mining scheme, two parallel open-pit mining faces will be opened and actively mined, advancing away from each other, throughout the life of the project. Fina, representing a group of companies, has also submitted an application to the Energy Resources Conservation Board (ERCB) for a permit to produce 122,500 bbl/day of synthetic crude oil by means of a scheme based on mining wheels, hot-water extraction, and fluid coking. © 1978, Elsevier Science & Technology. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: GEOLOGY.
entry.dc:creator: Hewett F.
entry.dc:description: The geological setting and the development of the Cassiar Asbestos Mine in British Columbia are detailed here, and estimates of the ore reserves contained in the Cassiar orebody are presented. Present information indicates an orebody of approximately 16,277,000 tons amenable to open-pit mining, but continued diamond drilling will be needed to accurately define total tonnage and grade. A program has been developed at the mine to provide the required information on a daily basis, and work is continuing on more effective dollar-value prediction methods.

entry.dc:title: Calculation of the External Field of Natural Grounding of Complex Shape.
entry.dc:creator: Mitropol'skaya S.O.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The advantages and disadvantages of the earlier methods of calculation of external fields and groundings of complex shape are considered. A new method of calculation of the external field of a grounding in the shape of a rectangular plate is proposed. The possibility of utilizing theoretically calculated external fields around mathematical models of complex groundings to predict electric safety conditions at open-pit mining works is demonstrated.

entry.dc:title: JACOBS RANCH SELECTS OPEN-PIT MINING PLAN.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: Kerr-McGee Coal Corp. 's open-pit mining project is featured that calls for production of 14. 5 million tons per year by the mid-1980's from the three seams at the company's Jacobs Ranch mine in Wyoming's Powder River Basin. The project will provide flexibility demanded by multiple seam mining, quick access to seams and lower reclamation activities and costs. Stripping, overburden removal, pit advances and reclamation steps are detailed.

entry.dc:title: LONG-RANGE MINE PLANNING AT GIBRALTAR MINES LIMITED.
entry.dc:creator: Milner T.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the package of computer programs implemented at Gibraltar Mines Ltd. (an open-pit copper mine) for the development of long-range mine plans. A Lerch-Grossman three-dimensional pit design program is used for pit design and sequencing of interior-stage pits. A mine simulation program is used to produce production schedules and open-pit mining equipment requirements. Discounted-cash-flow techniques are used to evaluate alternate mine plan schedules. Areas under consideration for further expansion of the computer mine design package will also be discussed.

entry.dc:title: PP&L'S PIT CONCEPT AIDS ANTHRACITE.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: Open-pit coal mining may be coming to the eastern U. S. under a new walking version that could make anthracite the ideal low-sulfur fuel for Pennsylvania. Power and Light Co's (PP&L) next generating plants. The firm's engineers, devising improvements in the conventional open-pit techniques, have come up with a walking version of open-pit mining in which land is reclaimed automatically behind the operation as the pit moves along in the direction of mining. Open land is thus kept to a minimum yet the pit is large enough to allow recovery of coal deeply from the multiple anthracite seams that generally exist in the area of the deposit.

entry.dc:title: APPLICATION OF THE METHOD OF QUEUEING THEORY TO DETERMINE THE DUMP-TRUCK CAPACITY FOR OPEN-PIT MINING OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Yamaguchi U.
entry.dc:description: In the open-pit limestone quarry which produces 6200 tons of limestone each day using the Caterpillar 988 (bucket capacity 4. 59 m**3) and 15 ton dump-trucks haulage system, queueing technique was applied to analyze the haulage operation. The suitable number of trucks for a 1000 meter haulage distance to the crusher from the working face of the quarry is 3 to 4 trucks to obtain the lowest haulage cost per ton of limestone.

entry.dc:title: HIBBING TACONITE STARTS UP PHASE I WITH NOTABLE MINING AND MILLING FEATURES.
entry.dc:creator: Sisselman R.
entry.dc:description: Key features of Hibbing Taconite Co. 's ongoing construction program in the Mesabi Range, Minn. , which will raise the initial design capacity of 5. 4 million ltpy of pellets to 8. 1 million ltpy by 1979, are briefly described here. The expansion project calls for some large open-pit mining equipment (most notably 170-ton ore haulage trucks and electric shovels equipped with 16-cu-yd dippers); single-stage, closed circuit crushing; single-stage, closed circuit grinding in 36-ft-diam, fully autogenous mills; and traveling grate pelletizing systems.

entry.dc:title: Opencast Mining of Coal in France.
entry.dc:creator: Iooss R.
entry.dc:description: The opencast mining method consists in removing the overburden situated above a coal deposit in order to exploit this deposit by the open-pit mining method. The author briefly examines the history of open cast mining of coal in France, and then describes the French coal deposits workable by this method. Proved reserves of these deposits, total 12 million tons, whereas possible reserves are estimated at 8 million tons. Technical details are given on the open cast mining method with particular reference to the type of machinery used, transport, land reclamation and minig costs.

entry.dc:title: LARGER ELECTRIC MINING SHOVEL OF THE FUTURE, TODAY.
entry.dc:creator: Burns S.
entry.dc:description: Shovels of 18 cubic yard capacity and larger are described which incorporate advanced technology and techniques providing performance and operation tailored to meet the needs of open-pit mining. To achieve the goals of increasing production at lower cost with consideration of maximum availability, lower energy consumption per ton and low impact on pit power, Harnischfeger Corporation developed a solid-state drive system ( ″Electrotorque″ - P&H trademark) and applied unique transmission methods. This paper discusses the electrical features and touches briefly on some mechanical features of this new shovel.

entry.dc:title: Reclamation: A Challenge to Open-Pit Mining in Canada..
entry.dc:creator: Zahary G.
entry.dc:description: Open-pit mine reclamation criteria of legal, technical and esthetic nature are reviewed. The types of solid wastes resulting from mining operations are described. The results of research on the possibility of implanting a vegetal cover on highly acidic siliceous residues produced by uranium ore treatment plants at Ellito Lake, Ontario, are presented, demonstrating the success of a program of soil ph neutralization and the addition of nutritive elements.

entry.dc:title: Foreseeable Developments of Mining Techniques in Large Coal-Producing Countries.
entry.dc:creator: Ellie G.
entry.dc:description: The research to improve the productivity of coal mining operations basically tend toward finding techniques for reducing the personnel, either by doing away with certain tasks, or by mechanizing and automating certain operations or, yet again, by improving the reliability of the methods and equipment. For conventionally mined deposits such as, first of all, strikes in which the coal is extracted by known open-pit mining processes and also shallow mines having regular horizontal layers, the advances made in modernizing the methods and to which the major world producers are devoting their efforts are especially in the design of cutting, transport and pit propping equipment in order to arrive at ″the less″ workings. The question of exploiting the large coal reserves in difficult and deep deposits is considered. Problems of operational strategy, remote control and monitoring of underground installations are indicated.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Bunch J.
entry.dc:description: Problems of permit issuance and renewal and trends in machinery use are discussed. Open-pit miners will continue to take a critical look at equipment replacement and utilization during 1977. Traditional mining methods may be replaced by new procedures which require less fuel and energy. The major consideration in equipment manufacturing will be operating economy rather than expanded capacity. Improved efficiency and economy are the main criteria for competitive extraction and processing of declining ore grades in 1977.

entry.dc:title: Radiation exposures associated with surface mining for uranium
entry.dc:creator: Miller H.
entry.dc:description: Measurements of external gamma radiation, radon and radon progeny, and airborne uranium aerosols were made at an operating open-pit mining operation using readily available field survey techniques and instruments. Measurement techniques are discussed. Radiation exposure to various occupational categories, such as excavation equipment operators, truck drivers, equipment maintenance personnel, ore control personnel, and to the engineering staff, is estimated. These estimates are compared to the results of film badge dosimetry. While the average exposure rate was found to be in the order of 0.5 mR/hr±0.5 mR/hr, it was noted that higher exposures (up to lOmR/hr) were measured in the vicinity of ore bodies containing uranium in the per cent range. Some contamination of earth-moving equipment by uranium-bearing dusts was also noted. © 1977 Health Physics Society.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT MINING IN POWDER RIVER.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: This article deals with Carter Mining Co. 's Rawhide mine, one of the newest and largest (designed for 12 million tpy) coal complexes in the Powder River Basin, which will begin producing coal by the open-pit method, using a truck/shovel/scraper combination. Adoption of the open-pit method was done to gain greater flexibility of operation, easier land reclamation and a reduction in the area of disturbed land. The mine will produce coal from two seams totaling 100 ft in thickness.

entry.dc:title: UNIQUE APPLICATION OF SEISMIC METHODS IN AN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Kim Y.S.
entry.dc:description: A feasibility seismic refraction and reflection field survey was conducted at the U. S. Borax Company open-pit mine, Boron, California by the writers during the weekend of March 13 and 14, 1976. This field survey was carried out as a preliminary investigation primarily for the purpose of evaluating and establishing the ability of such geophysical techniques to locate and outline the subsurface openings of the old room-and-pillar mining under the present open-pit. The value of such knowledge about the old underground workings is directly related to the safe and economical operation of the open-pit mine for the company.

entry.dc:title: MINING ENGINEERING - REVIEW/'75 MINING EXPLORATION MINERAL PROCESSING.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Summary reports with extensive bibliographics are presented on geology, geophysics, geochemistry, geological engineering, open-pit mining, underground mining, hydrology, solution mining, rock mechanics, operations research, mineral processing, crushing and grinding, concentration, hydrometallurgy, pyrolysis and agglomeration, materials handling, operating controls, and environmental control.

entry.dc:title: Hydraulic rock drills - their role in open pit mining.
entry.dc:creator: Durk R.
entry.dc:description: The author aims at outlining the present status of the hydraulic drill in the mining industry, both surface and underground. The operating principles of both the pneumatic percussion rock drill and the hydraulic rock drill are described and compared. It is considered that the advantages of the hydraulic rock drill are (i) better performance (ii) greater efficiency (iii) reduced specific energy requirements compared with the pneumatic drills (iv) reduced fuel requirements (v) less capital cost (vi) lower maintenance costs and reduced downtime (vii) better environmental conditions - reduced noise and other pollution. Hydraulic drills manufacturwd by Dresser Industries , Ingersoll-Rand , Eimco-Secoma and Atlas-Copco are described, together with performance characteristics. Applications of such hydraulic drills include road construction, open-pit mining activities (secondary blasting operations).

entry.dc:title: Computer Simulation of an Open-Pit Mining Process.
entry.dc:creator: Tarasiewicz S.
entry.dc:description: An approach to the way of forming a simulation model with the use of ″time slicing″ is presented. Before the simulation programmes are worked out the digital models of elementary units and technological structure configuration are formed. Then the model of technological process structure is represented in computer memory. As a result of this procedure a simulation programme for ODRA 1204 computer is worked out and tested. These programmes can be used to analyze mining technological processes of any open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: Ore-Dressing Combine of the Future with Open-Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Shafarenko I.
entry.dc:description: The project of a model ore-dressing combine of the future, envisaged for the Chernyanskoye iron ore deposit in the Kursk Magnetic Anomaly Basin is described. Lying under an overburden 160 m deep, its ore reserves down to the projected depth of the open-cast mine of 565 m amount to 1913 Mt, including 176 Mt of rich ore and 1737 Mt of ferrous quartzites. It is planned that the output of the first stage of the mine will be 60 Mt of quartzites and 8 Mt of rich ore. In the more distant future the output of quartzites will be 120 Mt p. a. The overburden rock will be dumped in ravines, covered with top soil, and handed over agricultural use. Slurry will be piped to distances of 10-15 km.

entry.dc:title: PIT SLOPE DISPLACEMENT MONITORING: AN AID TO OPEN-PIT MINE OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: MacRae A.
entry.dc:description: Slope failures exact a large, unpredictable sum from the open-pit mining industry every year, and fatalities and large-scale equipment damage are not the only forms of loss. Direct cost for removal of slide material is considerable, and indirects associated with rescheduling and lost production are significant over the long term. This article describes existing slope displacement monitoring systems and some new developments, including information on system accuracy, range, applicability, and cost, based on the author's past projects. Advantages and disadvantages of the systems are discussed, and suggestions are made for future improvements in this field.
